latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The previous prompt preserved object presence, flamingo count, turtle count, bicycle color, and the under relation, but it was too generic about the two hard attributes and too weak for reliably counting seven bicycles. 'Spotted flamingos' and 'glass turtles' were stated once, yet the scene framing emphasized the row relation more than making the spotted plumage and transparent glass material visually obvious. The bicycle count likely collapsed because a single row of seven bicycles encouraged overlap, truncation, or visual merging.
expected_improvement: Make the spotted pattern on each flamingo explicit and visually salient so the verifier can recognize all flamingos as spotted.
Make the turtles read clearly as glass by explicitly describing transparent glass material and visible light-through bodies.
Improve bicycle count accuracy by requiring exactly seven fully visible, separated black bicycles with side-by-side spacing and no extra bicycles.
preserve_constraints: Exactly three flamingos are present and fully visible.
Exactly seven black bicycles are present.
Each turtle is under a bicycle.
All required objects should remain distinct, countable, and unobstructed.

previous_plan_error.details: The plan relied on a single compact sentence for attribute binding and used one row for seven bicycles, which encouraged counting errors and did not force visually obvious spotted flamingos or clearly transparent glass turtles.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple wide composition with seven separated bicycle-turtle pairs across the image so each bicycle is individually countable and each turtle remains directly below its bicycle. Place the three flamingos separately in open space away from the bicycle row. Strengthen attribute binding by explicitly describing each flamingo as covered in visible spots and each turtle as made of transparent glass. Add negative clauses against extra bicycles and merged duplicates.
regression_risks: Tight spacing across seven bicycle-turtle pairs could cause overlap and reduce countability.
Strengthening turtle glass appearance could make turtles harder to see unless visibility is also emphasized.
Keeping flamingos separate from the bicycle row could regress if they become cropped or too small.
repair_constraints: Show exactly seven black bicycles, each fully visible and clearly separated from the others, with no extra bicycles.
Show exactly seven turtles directly underneath the seven bicycles, one turtle under each bicycle.
Bind glass material to the turtles explicitly: each turtle is made of transparent glass and visibly reads as glass.
Show exactly three flamingos, fully visible and separate from the bicycles and turtles.
Bind the spotted attribute to the flamingos explicitly: each flamingo has clearly visible spots on its body.
Keep all objects unobstructed, non-overlapping, and easy to count.
latest_teacher_action.retry_prompt: A clear wide scene with exactly seven black bicycles arranged side by side in a single spaced row, each bicycle fully visible and clearly separated from the others. Directly underneath each bicycle is exactly one turtle, for exactly seven turtles total, one turtle under each bicycle; each turtle is made of transparent glass and clearly looks like a glass turtle. Also show exactly three flamingos in the same scene, separate from the bicycle row and fully visible; each flamingo has clearly visible spots on its body and clearly looks spotted. Keep every bicycle, turtle, and flamingo distinct, unobstructed, complete, and easy to count. No extra bicycles, no extra turtles, no extra flamingos, no merged or overlapping duplicates.

skill_revision.reason: Persistent failures require stronger negative control against extra or merged bicycles, while retaining counting, attribute binding, spatial layout, and visibility skills.
